page: UpCloud DEV-2xCPU-8GB is a developer-class virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 2 vCPUs with a shared CPU allocation, meaning physical resources are shared among tenants. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with 80 GB of local SSD capacity, and the instance comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates that this server is positioned for entry-level workloads, with several performance limitations. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, both falling into the bottom 10% of benchmarks. Memory performance is also constrained, with passmark memory scores and large-block read-only memory bandwidth registering in the bottom 10%. However, the system achieves average performance in single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tests. Software compilation with Clang and static web serving throughput are weak, reflecting the resource-sharing model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a budget-friendly entry point for development and testing environments where continuous high-performance CPU execution is not required. The inclusion of 80 GB of local SSD storage and a public IPv4 address provides a complete basic environment without requiring separate storage provisioning. It is best suited for lightweight tasks such as software prototyping, running small development databases, executing basic scripts, or hosting low-traffic staging applications. It is not recommended for production databases, heavy compilation tasks, or high-throughput web serving.
